thread:
Maya L: handing off 3rd shift — I'm on until 7am PT. Quick rundown:
- Deployments: rolled v3.12 to staging at 02:10, no regressions observed; canary 10% traffic. Watch models: gpt-small-q4 & redwood/opt-2.9. Latency looks fine but q4 has occasional 10-20ms p50 spikes.
- Active alerts: none. Alerting thresholds tightened for token spooler — see alert: token-spooler-queue > 300
- Known risk: KV-cache memory growth on low-traffic pods after long-running streams. Restarting pods clears it. I've left a cron restart at 04:30 for the next 3 days.
- Action items: Jordan to finish the batching rollout at 10am PT; Liam to validate canary fallback rule.
- Oncall handoff docs: https://internal.redwood/handoff/docs (link)

Jordan T: Thanks! Quick Q: what's the exact canary weight? I saw 10% but the deploy notes say 7.5%

Maya L: We bumped to 10% after smoke passed. My bad on the notes, updated the deploy description.

Priya S: FYI there's a large tenant import running in prod starting 05:00 PT — it increases request fanout, watch queues.

Liam K: I'll keep an eye on node cpu and spooler. If queues > 200 I'll scale dedicated-pool3 by +2 replicas (cmd: `kubectl scale deploy dedicated-pool3 --replicas=5`)

oncall-bot: Incident-free for 72 hours :tada:

Jordan T: pinging @Maya L for the PR that modifies batching config so I can review before my window.

Maya L: PR #4582 in github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4582 — it's small, mostly config; tests passing.

Priya S: Also note: nightly backup window moves from 03:00 -> 04:30 for this week. Could bump latency during snapshot.

Liam K: Copy. I'll set a watcher on snapshot metrics and slack alarms.

Maya L: Thanks team — leaving notes in oncall doc. I'm reachable on call if needed. /handoff complete :white_check_mark:
